title: Brand and customers
purpose: When I am about to brief an ad, a page, an email or a product and cannot say who buys from us and why, open Customers to see the real buyers, their own words, their doubts and what each group is worth.
fires: The persona deck made once and never updated, the agency's guess at the customer, the founder's memory of who buys, and the habit of not talking to customers.
not_for: A store with under about 200 orders and no reviews yet; there is not enough evidence, and 10 phone calls with buyers will beat any screen.

jobs.job: When I brief an ad, a page or a product and cannot say who buys from us and why, show me the real buyers and their reasons, backed by orders, reviews and their own words, so money stops going to a customer we made up
jobs.circumstance: A new campaign brief is due, the agency asks "who is the target?", and the persona deck is 2 years old

progress.functional: know the 2 or 3 buyer groups, what each is trying to get done, and each group's share of revenue
progress.emotional: stop the unease of guessing who we sell to
progress.social: give the agency and team a customer they can trust and quote

jobs.hire_today: the founder's memory, an old persona deck, or the agency's guess
jobs.fire: the persona deck and the "women 25 to 45" target

forces.push: ads aimed at a made-up customer waste budget
forces.pull: buyer groups with proof and a revenue share each
forces.anxiety: what if the groups are wrong and the team builds on them

jobs.little_hire: before every brief, and each quarter

watch.metric: share of last 90 days' revenue from buyer groups backed by at least 5 real quotes
watch.source: Shopify orders, reviews and surveys in the brand brain

drives.metric: conversion rate on ads built for a named buyer group, 14 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 percent of revenue is tied to a buyer group with proof. After: 70 percent within 60 days.
jobs.not_for: a brand with a single, obvious buyer that the whole team already knows by name

jobs.job: When plenty of people visit and few buy, name the top reasons they hold back and what changed the mind of those who did buy, so the page answers the doubt instead of shouting louder
jobs.circumstance: Product page conversion stuck at 1.8 percent, heavy traffic, and no idea what stops people

progress.functional: know the top 3 doubts and the proof that removed each one
progress.social: brief the designer and copywriter with evidence

jobs.hire_today: a conversion freelancer, a survey pop-up nobody reads, or guessing

forces.push: traffic is expensive and most of it leaves
forces.pull: each doubt paired with the thing that removed it
forces.habit: we add more reviews and badges
forces.anxiety: what if the doubts we find are not the ones that matter

watch.metric: product page add to cart rate, 14 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: sizing doubt shows up in 30 percent of pre-sale chats, with no answer on the page. After: a fit guide and a buyer's quote go up, and add to cart rises 12 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store whose problem is too little traffic, not too few buyers

jobs.job: When a new wave of reviews comes in, tell me what customers love and hate and whether it is getting better or worse, so a quality slip does not hurt sales before I see it
jobs.circumstance: 300 new reviews a month, the average star is steady, but 1-star reviews about a seam are rising

progress.functional: know review themes, their trend and their effect on stars, month by month
progress.emotional: stop fearing what I have not read
progress.social: go to the supplier with proof of a quality problem

jobs.hire_today: the support lead's summary, or nobody reading them
jobs.fire: the average star as the only check

forces.push: a hidden quality slip spreads into returns and ratings
forces.pull: themes and trends, with quotes
forces.habit: we look at the star average
forces.anxiety: what if a few loud reviews skew the themes

watch.metric: share of 1 to 2 star reviews by theme, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: seam complaints rose from 2 to 9 percent over 3 months, unseen. After: they are flagged at 4 percent and the supplier fixes it.
jobs.not_for: a store with fewer than 20 reviews a month, where the owner can read them all

jobs.job: When returns and support tickets climb, find the top reasons behind them in customers' own words, so we fix the cause and not just refund
jobs.circumstance: Return rate up from 8 to 12 percent, reasons coded "other", and support drowning

progress.functional: know return and ticket reasons, ranked by cost
progress.emotional: stop the frustration of paying for the same problem again and again
progress.social: give the supplier, designer and page team a clear fix list

jobs.hire_today: the support lead's sense, or the returns app's reason codes

forces.push: returns cost shipping both ways and the sale
forces.pull: reasons ranked by dollars, with quotes
forces.anxiety: what if the reasons customers give are not the real ones

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and when the return rate jumps

watch.metric: share of returns and tickets by reason, with cost, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 12 percent returns, 40 percent coded "other". After: "runs small" is found as 45 percent of returns, the size chart is fixed, and returns fall to 9 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store with a return rate under 2 percent

jobs.job: When an agency or freelancer writes ads, pages or emails in our name, check they sound like us and only say what is true, so I stop reading every line myself
jobs.circumstance: 20 new ads a week from the agency, and the founder reviews each one at night

progress.functional: know which drafts break our voice or make claims we cannot prove
progress.emotional: let go of line-by-line review without fear
progress.social: give the agency clear notes, not taste

jobs.hire_today: the founder as the reviewer of everything

forces.push: hours a week, and the founder becomes the bottleneck
forces.pull: drafts checked against our voice and our proof before they reach me
forces.anxiety: what if something off-brand or untrue slips through

watch.metric: new ads, pages and emails that pass the voice and proof check before launch, and founder review hours

drives.metric: live claims with no proof on file

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 5 hours a week reviewing drafts. After: 1 hour, and no unproven claim goes live.
jobs.not_for: a founder who writes all the copy alone

jobs.job: When I or the copywriter sit down to write an ad, a page or an email, give me the exact words customers use for the problem and the result, so the copy sounds like them and not like us
jobs.circumstance: A blank ad brief, a copywriter writing "premium comfort", and reviews full of better phrases no one reads

progress.functional: have a ranked list of real customer phrases by topic
progress.emotional: stop the cringe of copy that sounds like every brand
progress.social: give the copywriter material that makes their work better

jobs.hire_today: a copywriter reading reviews, or brainstorming

forces.push: generic copy costs clicks
forces.pull: real phrases, ranked by how often buyers say them
forces.habit: we write in our brand voice
forces.anxiety: what if customer words sound rough or off-brand

jobs.little_hire: every brief and every copy round

watch.metric: click rate on ads using a customer phrase against ads that do not, 14 day
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, brand brain phrase list

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 in 10 ads uses a customer phrase. After: 6 in 10, with click rate up 20 percent on those.
jobs.not_for: a brand whose buyers never write reviews or tickets, so there are no words to mine yet

jobs.job: When I decide where to spend to win new buyers, show me which buyer groups make the most gross profit over 6 months, not just the biggest first order, so budget goes to buyers worth having
jobs.circumstance: Planning next quarter's ad budget, and first-order value is the only number we have

progress.functional: know gross profit per customer at 180 days, by buyer group and first product
progress.emotional: stop spending blind on first-order numbers
progress.social: defend budget moves to a partner or the agency

jobs.hire_today: a finance lead's cohort sheet, or nobody
jobs.fire: first-order return as the budget rule

forces.push: cheap first orders from buyers who never come back
forces.pull: profit per group over time
forces.anxiety: what if 180 days is too short for our rebuy cycle

watch.metric: gross profit per customer at 180 days, by buyer group and first product
watch.source: Shopify orders, product costs in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: budget is split evenly. After: 60 percent goes to the group worth $48 at 180 days, against $19 for the other.
jobs.not_for: a store under 6 months old, with no 180 day history yet

jobs.job: When new buyers arrive, learn what made them choose us, where they first heard of us and what they stopped using, so I know what is really bringing them in
jobs.circumstance: New customers are up, attribution says Meta, but buyers say "a friend told me"

progress.functional: know first-heard source, reason to buy and what they switched from
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: Nothing, or a post-purchase survey app nobody reads. The answers pile up untagged
jobs.fire: platform attribution as the only story

forces.push: we credit the wrong channel and fund it
forces.pull: buyers' own answers, grouped and counted
forces.anxiety: what if survey answers are lazy picks

watch.metric: share of new customers by stated reason and first place heard, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: all credit goes to Meta. After: 30 percent say word of mouth, so referral gets budget.
jobs.not_for: a store with too few orders a month for survey answers to add up

jobs.job: When "not as expected" returns keep coming, help me say clearly who the product is wrong for, so the wrong buyers stop buying and returning
jobs.circumstance: Buyers expecting a thick winter sock get a thin running sock and send it back

progress.functional: know which buyers return most and why, and write the "not for" line
progress.emotional: accept that fewer, happier buyers is fine
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. Saying "not for you" feels like losing sales, so no one does it

forces.push: wrong buyers cost returns and bad reviews
forces.pull: a clear "not for" line, with the return cost it saves
forces.anxiety: what if saying who it is not for drops sales

jobs.little_hire: when a product's returns run high

watch.metric: returns marked "not as expected" or "did not suit", 60 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 6 percent of orders are returned as not as expected. After: 3 percent, after a "not for" line on the page.
jobs.not_for: a product that suits nearly everyone, like a phone charger

jobs.job: When reviews and chats say "too expensive", tell me whether buyers mean they cannot afford it or do not see the value, so I fix the right thing instead of cutting price
jobs.circumstance: "Too pricey" in 8 percent of chats, and the team wants a discount

progress.functional: know what buyers compare our price to, and what value they miss
progress.social: push back on the discount ask with evidence

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, or a discount test

forces.push: discounts cost margin on every order
forces.pull: price doubts sorted by cause
forces.anxiety: what if the buyers really cannot afford it

watch.metric: share of chats and reviews naming price, split by "cannot afford" and "not worth it", 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 15 percent discount is planned. After: value is shown against a cheaper rival's lifespan, no discount runs, conversion holds and margin is kept.
jobs.not_for: a budget brand that competes on lowest price by design

jobs.job: When bad comments or tickets about one topic spike, tell me the same day, so I answer before it spreads
jobs.circumstance: A batch arrived damaged, and 15 comments landed on Instagram in 3 hours

progress.functional: know the spike, the topic and how big it is against normal
progress.emotional: stop being the last to know
progress.social: answer in public before it becomes a story

jobs.hire_today: a social media manager, or nobody
jobs.fire: finding out from a customer tagging us

forces.push: spreading complaints cost sales and trust
forces.pull: an early warning with the topic named
forces.anxiety: what if it fires for every small moan

watch.metric: negative comments and tickets on one topic in 24 hours, against normal

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a damaged batch was found after 3 days and 60 complaints. After: it is found in 3 hours and replacements go out.
jobs.not_for: a brand with a full-time community manager watching every comment

jobs.job: When I plan retention, show me which buyer groups come back and which buy once, so I spend to win more of the ones who return
jobs.circumstance: Repeat rate is 22 percent overall, and some groups are likely much higher

progress.functional: know repeat rate at 90 days by buyer group and first product
progress.social: brief the email team on who to invest in

jobs.hire_today: a retention freelancer's report, or nobody

forces.push: we spend the same to win buyers worth very different amounts
forces.pull: repeat rate per group
forces.anxiety: what if the groups are too small to trust

watch.metric: repeat purchase rate at 90 days by buyer group
watch.source: Shopify orders, buyer groups in the brand brain

drives.metric: gross profit per customer at 180 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: one 22 percent repeat rate. After: gift buyers at 8 percent and athletes at 38, so budget shifts to athletes.
jobs.not_for: a one-time-purchase product, where almost no one comes back by nature

jobs.job: When new ads keep failing and the agency wants to change settings, tell me whether our buyers or their doubts have changed, so we fix the message and not the knobs
jobs.circumstance: 6 weeks of failed creative tests, and the agency keeps tweaking audiences and budgets

progress.functional: check if buyer groups, their words or their doubts have moved
progress.emotional: stop the helpless feeling of tests that all fail
progress.social: redirect the agency with a reason

jobs.hire_today: the agency's settings changes

forces.push: a stall wastes weeks of test budget
forces.pull: a fresh read of the buyer
forces.anxiety: what if it is a settings problem after all

jobs.little_hire: when 4 or more tests fail in a row

watch.metric: share of new ads that beat the account's median click rate, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 of 8 new ads beat the median. After: a new doubt is found, and 3 of 6 beat it.
jobs.not_for: a store with no paid ads

jobs.job: When it costs more each quarter to win a new customer, tell me which buyer groups are getting pricier to reach and which are still cheap, so budget moves to where buyers cost less
jobs.circumstance: Blended cost per new customer is up 25 percent in a year

progress.functional: know cost per new customer by buyer group, each quarter
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: the agency's audience report

forces.push: rising cost to win buyers squeezes margin
forces.pull: cost by group, with the trend
forces.anxiety: what if the split of ad results by group is rough

watch.metric: cost per new customer by buyer group, 28 day
watch.source: ad platforms, Shopify, buyer groups in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $38 blended. After: $31, after 30 percent of budget moves to the cheaper group.
jobs.not_for: a store that wins most buyers without paid ads

jobs.job: When good customers stop buying, ask them why in their own words, so we learn what we broke or who took them
jobs.circumstance: 30 percent of last year's repeat buyers have not bought in 9 months

progress.functional: know why lapsed buyers left and where they went
progress.emotional: face the loss instead of guessing
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. No one calls lapsed buyers, because it is awkward and slow
jobs.fire: a win-back discount sent without knowing why they left

forces.push: lost repeat buyers are the costliest loss
forces.pull: reasons from the people who left
forces.anxiety: what if they do not reply

watch.metric: lapsed buyers who gave a reason, and share of reasons by theme, quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a win-back code only, with 3 percent coming back. After: the reasons are found, a fix is made, and 8 percent come back.
jobs.not_for: a one-time-purchase product, where no one is expected to come back

jobs.job: When one ad works for some buyers and flops for others, help me split our one broad customer into groups with their own reasons to buy, so each gets a message that fits
jobs.circumstance: The same socks are bought by runners, by nurses on long shifts and as gifts, and one ad tries to talk to all of them

progress.functional: see which buyers have a different reason to buy, and each group's revenue
progress.social: brief the agency with groups, not one blur

jobs.hire_today: an agency strategist, or one broad message

forces.push: one message for everyone converts no one well
forces.pull: groups with their own words and value
forces.anxiety: what if we split too fine and spread budget thin

jobs.little_hire: when results split, or each quarter

watch.metric: buyer groups with their own reason to buy, quote set and revenue share

drives.metric: cost per purchase on group-specific ads, 14 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 group. After: 3 groups, with ads per group cutting cost per purchase 18 percent.
jobs.not_for: a niche product with one clear buyer and one reason to buy

jobs.job: When a new agency, freelancer or hire starts, hand them who our customer is in one place, so I do not explain it from scratch again
jobs.circumstance: Third agency in 2 years, and each starts with a "discovery phase" I pay for

progress.functional: give a new partner the buyer groups, words, doubts and proof on day 1
progress.emotional: stop the fatigue of repeating myself
progress.social: look organised to a new partner

jobs.hire_today: calls, old decks, or paying for their discovery phase
jobs.fire: the paid discovery phase and the repeat briefing calls

forces.push: every new partner costs weeks of ramp-up
forces.pull: one current customer file
forces.anxiety: what if the file is out of date and misleads them

watch.metric: days from a partner's start to their first live work

drives.metric: agency and freelance cost per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 4 weeks of discovery at $6k. After: first live work in week 1.
jobs.not_for: a founder who does all the work and hires no one

jobs.job: When I have not spoken to a customer in months because the business got busy, get me a steady flow of short customer conversations, so I hear the struggle and not just the numbers
jobs.circumstance: The founder used to answer every email, and now it has been 6 months without a real customer talk

progress.functional: have 2 to 4 customer talks a month, with notes that feed the brand brain
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: Nothing, or rare calls. Booking them is a chore and feels awkward

forces.push: owners drift from customers as the store grows
forces.pull: talks booked and notes kept for me
forces.anxiety: what if customers feel sold to on the call

watch.metric: customer talks logged per month

drives.metric: new findings added to buyer groups per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 talks in 6 months. After: 3 a month, with 2 new doubts found in the first quarter.
jobs.not_for: a founder who still answers every customer email personally

jobs.job: When I have a new message or product idea, test it on real customers before spending on ads, so I do not pay to learn what 20 buyers could have told me
jobs.circumstance: A new angle for a campaign, with $10k about to go behind it

progress.functional: know if buyers understand the message and want it
progress.emotional: go into spend with more certainty
progress.social: bring the agency a message already checked

jobs.hire_today: a creative strategist's hunch, or spending and seeing

forces.push: failed campaigns are expensive lessons
forces.pull: fast answers from real buyers
forces.anxiety: what if a small group misleads us

watch.metric: share of new ads that beat the account's median click rate in 7 days

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 in 5 new angles beats the median. After: 2 in 5, after a check with buyers.
jobs.not_for: a brand whose ad tests are so cheap that testing live is faster

jobs.job: When the category feels crowded and ad costs keep rising, find a buyer group nobody else is chasing, so we win buyers who are not already bombarded by rivals
jobs.circumstance: Cost per purchase up 30 percent in a year, and every rival targets the same buyer

progress.functional: find a group with a real struggle, enough people and no brand talking to them
progress.emotional: see a way forward other than paying more
progress.social: bring the agency a fresh direction

jobs.hire_today: an agency strategist or consultant
jobs.fire: fighting for the same buyer as everyone

forces.push: the crowded buyer costs more every quarter
forces.pull: a new group with proof and size
forces.habit: we target our best current buyer
forces.anxiety: what if the group is too small

jobs.little_hire: when cost per purchase rises 2 quarters in a row

watch.metric: cost per purchase on ads built for the new group, 14 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $42 per purchase on the crowded group. After: $29 on the new one.
jobs.not_for: a brand still winning its main buyer at a good cost

jobs.job: When I am sure I know why people buy, show me where customers describe us differently than we describe ourselves, so I stop building on my own belief
jobs.circumstance: Our homepage leads with "sustainable", and reviews talk about comfort and fit

progress.functional: compare our main message with the words customers use
progress.emotional: face the gap without feeling wrong
progress.social: bring the team back to what customers value

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. The founder's view is rarely checked, because no one on the team wants to tell the founder they are wrong
jobs.fire: the founder's belief as the brief

forces.push: messaging that misses what buyers value
forces.pull: our words and theirs side by side
forces.anxiety: what if it says our founding story does not matter to buyers

watch.metric: share of review and survey words matching our main message, quarter
watch.source: reviews, surveys and site copy in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 12 percent of reviews mention our main message. After: the message changes to what 48 percent mention, and conversion rises 8 percent.
jobs.not_for: a new brand with too few reviews to compare against

jobs.job: When campaigns come and go, tell me if the brand itself is getting stronger or weaker, so I know if we are building something or renting sales
jobs.circumstance: Revenue swings with ad spend, and I cannot tell if people seek us out more than a year ago

progress.functional: know branded search, direct visits and word of mouth against last year
progress.emotional: know the business has value beyond this month's ads
progress.social: show investors the brand is growing, with proof

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. Brand tracking studies cost too much for a small store, so no one tracks it
jobs.fire: judging the brand by this month's sales

forces.push: a brand that weakens costs more to sell every year
forces.pull: a brand health line over time
forces.anxiety: what if the signals are too noisy to read

watch.metric: branded search clicks, 4 weeks against the same weeks last year

drives.metric: share of revenue from direct and branded visits

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no view. After: branded search up 22 percent on last year, shown in the investor update.
jobs.not_for: a store selling mostly on marketplaces, where buyers rarely search the brand name

jobs.job: When the team still quotes customer research from a year ago, recheck who buys against fresh orders and reviews, so we are not selling to last year's customer
jobs.circumstance: Research was done at launch, and the buyer mix has shifted with new channels

progress.functional: know if the buyer groups still hold and what moved
progress.emotional: stop the doubt about old research
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. Research is done once and never rerun, because it felt finished

forces.push: stale research misleads every brief
forces.pull: a check every quarter showing what changed
forces.anxiety: what if the refresh contradicts what we built on

watch.metric: buyer groups rechecked against orders and reviews in the last 90 days

drives.metric: share of revenue from buyer groups backed by fresh proof

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: groups were last checked 14 months ago. After: they are rechecked every quarter, and one new group is found.
jobs.not_for: a store under a year old, where the first research is still fresh

jobs.job: When a big share of orders are gifts, tell me who buys and who uses, so gift season ads speak to the giver and the product still pleases the person who gets it
jobs.circumstance: 35 percent of fourth-quarter orders are gifts, and the ads talk to the wearer

progress.functional: know the gift share and what givers care about
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, or last year's gift guide
jobs.fire: one message for giver and user

forces.push: gift buyers have their own doubts, like size and returns
forces.pull: a giver profile with words and timing
forces.habit: gift season uses the same ads
forces.anxiety: what if gift buyers are too scattered to target

watch.metric: share of orders marked as gifts, and gift buyer conversion rate, 30 day
watch.source: Shopify order notes and gift options

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: gift buyers convert at 1.2 percent. After: a gift page and ads for givers lift it to 1.8.
jobs.not_for: a product almost no one buys as a gift

jobs.job: When I plan the calendar of ads and emails, tell me the moments that make someone buy, like a new job, a race, a season or a gift date, so messages land when buyers are ready
jobs.circumstance: Emails go out on a fixed weekly schedule, and sales cluster around moments we have not named

progress.functional: know the moments that trigger a purchase, and when they come
progress.social: brief the email and ad team with dates

jobs.hire_today: an email freelancer's hunch, or the retail calendar

forces.push: messages that miss the moment get ignored
forces.pull: named moments with timing
forces.anxiety: what if the moments are too personal to time

jobs.little_hire: each quarter and before seasonal planning

watch.metric: email click rate on messages timed to a buying moment, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: every send goes on a Tuesday. After: 4 timed moments, with email revenue up 15 percent.
jobs.not_for: an impulse product bought at any moment

jobs.job: When I am about to pay a creator, check their audience looks like our buyers, so the fee reaches people who could buy
jobs.circumstance: A creator quotes $5,000, has a big following, and I am not sure it is our buyer

progress.functional: know the overlap between their audience and our buyer groups
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: the creator's media kit, an influencer agency, or gut feel

forces.push: creator fees are wasted on the wrong audience
forces.pull: an audience check against our groups
forces.anxiety: what if the check rules out a creator who would work

watch.metric: cost per purchase from creator posts, 14 day
watch.source: discount codes and links in Shopify

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 of 5 creators did not pay back. After: 2 of 5 are skipped and the other 3 pay back.
jobs.not_for: a brand that does not pay creators

jobs.job: When shoppers search our site or ask support for something we do not have, collect what they were after, so we know what buyers want that we are not giving them
jobs.circumstance: Site search shows "wide", "kids" and "wool" often, with no results

progress.functional: know the top unmet searches and requests
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. Site search logs are never read, because no one owns them and the app hides them

forces.push: buyers leave to find it elsewhere
forces.pull: a monthly list of unmet requests
forces.anxiety: what if the searches come from browsers, not buyers

watch.metric: site searches with no result, and exits after them, 30 day

drives.metric: conversion rate on sessions that use search

jobs.job: When a rival or a cheaper option launches, tell me how easily our buyers would switch and what keeps them with us, so I protect what makes them stay
jobs.circumstance: A cheaper rival launched, and I do not know if our buyers care

progress.functional: know what holds buyers to us, and how many name a rival as an option
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: gut feel

forces.push: buyers who switch cost the most to win back
forces.pull: reasons to stay, ranked, with the share at risk
forces.anxiety: what if buyers say they are loyal and leave anyway

jobs.little_hire: when a rival launches or cuts price

watch.metric: share of repeat buyers who name a rival as an option in surveys, quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: we matched a rival's price at once. After: a survey shows 10 percent at risk, so we hold price and send a loyalty perk.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no real rivals for its buyers

jobs.job: When customers use the product in ways we never planned, find those uses in reviews and chats, so we open new angles and reach new buyers
jobs.circumstance: Reviews mention using our socks for hospital shifts and hiking

progress.functional: know the unplanned uses and how many buyers name them
progress.social: none

forces.push: new angles hide in plain sight
forces.pull: uses counted, with quotes
forces.habit: we market the use we built for
forces.anxiety: what if it is a tiny group

watch.metric: share of reviews naming an unplanned use

drives.metric: revenue from ads or pages built on the new use

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 ads for shift workers. After: 2 ads, with cost per purchase 20 percent under the account.
jobs.not_for: a product with one narrow use that cannot be marketed beyond it

jobs.job: When new words or needs start showing up in reviews, chats and searches, catch them early, so we lead with them before rivals do
jobs.circumstance: "Blister" and "compression" appear more in reviews each month

progress.functional: know which phrases are rising in customer talk, month by month
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. No one tracks how customer words change, because it means rereading thousands of reviews each month

forces.push: late to a need buyers already voice
forces.pull: rising phrases with counts
forces.habit: we use the words we have always used
forces.anxiety: what if a rise comes from one batch of reviews

watch.metric: phrases rising in reviews, chats and site search for 3 months running

drives.metric: click rate on ads using the rising phrase, 14 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no view. After: "blister" is found rising, and a new ad using it beats the median by 25 percent.

jobs.job: When a few interviews or reviews point to a big finding, check it holds for many buyers before we rebuild around it, so we do not change course on 5 voices
jobs.circumstance: 5 interviews say buyers want a bigger pack, and we are about to change the range

progress.functional: know how many buyers agree, from 200 or more answers
progress.social: bring the team a finding with numbers

jobs.hire_today: Nothing, or a survey tool nobody sets up, because the story already feels true and the team wants to move
jobs.fire: acting on a handful of stories

forces.push: a wrong change of course costs a season
forces.pull: a count from real buyers
forces.anxiety: what if the survey wording leads the answers

jobs.little_hire: before any big change based on research

watch.metric: share of survey answers that confirm the finding, with at least 200 replies

drives.metric: gross profit from changes made on confirmed findings

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a pack change is made on 5 interviews. After: a 300-reply check shows only 20 percent agree, so the change is skipped.
jobs.not_for: a store with too few buyers to reach 200 answers

jobs.job: When we start selling in a new country, tell me whether buyers there want the same thing as buyers at home, so we do not run home-country messages to a different buyer
jobs.circumstance: 15 percent of orders now come from a second country, and the same ads run everywhere

progress.functional: compare buyer reasons, words and doubts by country
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: gut feel, or a local freelancer

forces.push: the wrong message wastes the new market's budget
forces.pull: buyer groups split by country
forces.anxiety: what if the data from the new country is too thin

jobs.little_hire: when a country passes 10 percent of orders

watch.metric: conversion rate by country on local messages, 30 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the UK converts at half the US rate. After: UK doubts are answered and the gap is halved.
jobs.not_for: a store that sells in one country only

jobs.job: When a buyer group we used to win is shrinking in our sales, tell me whether it is shrinking in the market too or going to someone else, so I know if we are losing them
jobs.circumstance: Gift buyers are down 20 percent for us this year

progress.functional: know our share of each group against that group's market trend
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: Nothing. No one splits share by buyer group, because it needs buyer groups and market data joined, and neither exists

forces.push: losing a group quietly shrinks the base
forces.pull: our trend against the group's trend
forces.anxiety: what if the group split in our data is rough

watch.metric: revenue by buyer group against the group's market demand, quarter
watch.source: buyer groups in the brand brain, search trends

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: gift buyers are down 20 percent while gift searches rose 5 percent. After: the gap is seen and the gift offer is rebuilt.
jobs.not_for: a store with one buyer group

jobs.job: When I think about a new product or partner, tell me what else our buyers buy and love, so the next move follows our customer and not a trend
jobs.circumstance: Surveys and reviews mention other brands our buyers use

progress.functional: know the brands and categories our buyers also buy
progress.social: find partners our buyers already like

jobs.hire_today: Nothing, or a guess, because no one asks buyers what else they buy

forces.push: easy growth next door goes to someone else
forces.pull: a list from our buyers' own answers
forces.anxiety: what if the survey sample is skewed

watch.metric: share of surveyed buyers naming each other category or brand

drives.metric: revenue from partner or next-door products

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no data. After: 40 percent of buyers name a running shoe brand, and a joint offer brings in 600 new buyers.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no plans for new products or partners

jobs.job: When I plan growth, tell me whether the number of people with the problem we solve is growing or shrinking, so I know how many new buyers are out there
jobs.circumstance: Growth is slowing, and the team asks if we have run out of buyers

progress.functional: know the size and trend of the buyer pool for each group
progress.emotional: know whether the ceiling is real
progress.social: none

jobs.hire_today: Nothing, or a guess from total market figures, because no one sizes the pool by buyer group

forces.push: a shrinking pool means rising ad costs
forces.pull: a buyer pool trend for each group
forces.habit: find more buyers with more spend
forces.anxiety: what if pool size estimates are too rough

watch.metric: search demand for each group's problem terms, quarter against last year
watch.source: search trend data in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: no view. After: the runner pool is flat and the shift worker pool is up 25 percent, so budget moves.
jobs.not_for: a brand far from any ceiling, still growing fast in its first buyer group
